program_overview.title: Swift and iOS Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: The Apple stack learned honestly: Swift to real depth, SwiftUI as the future it already is, and a capstone app built to App Store discipline.
program_overview.description:
iOS development is one of the most rewarding specializations in software, and it deserves an honest course: Swift learned as a real language, optionals, value types, protocols and concurrency understood properly, then iOS built the modern way with SwiftUI, architecture and state done right, data persistence, networking, and the production habits that make apps feel like Apple apps. A finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

One honesty first: serious iOS development requires a Mac, Xcode runs only on macOS. This course says so upfront (see the FAQ for the realistic options) rather than discovering it for you in week three. With that settled, the pace is honest too: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.
what_makes_this_different: The Mac requirement stated upfront, with realistic options, honesty most iOS courses skip
Swift as a language first: optionals, value semantics, protocols and structured concurrency understood properly
SwiftUI-first: the declarative future Apple is already building on
Apple-feel as a standard: human interface habits taught alongside code
An honest 10-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What does this Swift and iOS course cover?
faqs.answer: Swift as a real language first, optionals, value types, protocols and structured concurrency, then modern iOS with SwiftUI: views and state, navigation, architecture, persistence, networking, testing and App Store discipline, ending with a capstone app and the final exam. SwiftUI-first throughout, because that is where Apple and hiring are already going.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn Swift and iOS properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the language and its real-world domain; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Do I really need a Mac?
faqs.answer: Yes, honestly: Xcode runs only on macOS, and pretending otherwise wastes students’ money. Realistic options: any Apple-silicon Mac including used M1 machines handles the whole course; some students share a family Mac for practice sessions. If a Mac is out of reach right now, our React Native-based app course builds cross-platform apps from any laptop, and this course will still be here.

faqs.question: Swift or React Native for mobile?
faqs.answer: Native Swift wins when you want the Apple platform mastered deeply, the best performance and feel, and access to every new framework the day it ships. React Native wins for one-codebase-both-platforms from any laptop. We teach both roads honestly; this is the native-depth one.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, with 2 live classes a week in batches capped at 10 learners. A mini batch of 3-4 learners is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International learners pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.
